steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Choreographic intention is the purpose or message behind a dance — what the choreographer wants to communicate

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Every choreographic decision should serve the intention, from movement choices to structure and staging

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mood is the atmosphere or feeling a dance creates — for example, tense, joyful, melancholic

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Meaning is the deeper message or idea the dance conveys to the audience

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is choreographic intention? | Q: How do motifs help communicate choreographic intention? | Q: Why might an audience interpret a dance differently from the choreographer's intention?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Choreographic intention is the purpose or message the choreographer wants to communicate through the dance — it guides every creative decision. | Motifs are key movement phrases that embody the core idea. By developing and varying motifs throughout the dance, the choreographer reinforces the intention so the audience recognises and understands  | Each audience member brings their own experiences and perspectives, so they may understand the movement in a different way. Multiple interpretations are valid and enrich the dance.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always state the choreographic intention clearly before analysing how it is communicated Use specific movement examples to show how intention is conveyed — do not be vague Remember that mood and meaning are different — mood is atmosphere, meaning is the deeper idea In NEA tasks, write your intention as a clear statement and refer back to it throughout For professional works, quote the choreographer's stated intention and link it to what you see
